stories.name: Semiconductor stock comparisons
stories.blurb: A series of headlines comparing which semiconductor and AI chip stocks are the better buy for 2026 and beyond.

stories.name: Memory Chip Rally
stories.blurb: A surge in memory-chip and semiconductor stocks driven by booming AI demand for HBM and shifting industry dynamics.

stories.name: TSMC Revenue Surge
stories.blurb: TSMC's revenue and stock have been surging on strong AI chip demand, prompting analysts to debate whether the stock's rally reflects its true growth potential.

stories.name: TSMC Advanced Chip Expansion
stories.blurb: TSMC is investing in next-generation EUV lithography, advanced packaging, and U.S. manufacturing to meet surging AI chip demand and stay ahead of rivals like Intel and Samsung.

past.name: ASML High-NA EUV Deals
past.blurb: Chipmakers TSMC, Samsung and Intel commit to ASML's next-generation High-NA EUV lithography machines, boosting ASML's stock and outlook amid surging AI chip demand.

past.name: TSMC Intel chip race
past.blurb: TSMC and Intel are competing over advanced chip packaging, pricing, and foundry dominance as customers like Apple and AMD weigh their options.

events.name: ASML inks EUV deals with TSMC, Samsung

7.text: TSMC is cited as the dominant foundry with 72.5% of global revenue and an "unbreachable moat," and is recommended as a top AI stock for October. Several comparison articles weigh TSMC against Broadcom and Applied Materials as a 2026 investment.

8.text: Asian chip stocks rose on Micron's strong results and softer U.S. inflation, while FormFactor jumped on a Deutsche Bank Buy rating and Qualcomm fell on a Samsung 2nm pricing standoff. Onto Innovation and semiconductor winners/losers round out the coverage; TSMC is not directly mentioned.

6.text: TSMC is expected to post strong Q3 earnings on AI demand, with shares hitting a 52-week high and analysts projecting continued growth. Reports also say it is weighing a multibillion-dollar Texas chip campus beyond its Arizona investment.

9.text: TSMC may boost 2nm output, helping equipment makers, and holds 42% of the Foundry 2.0 market. Elon Musk confirmed preliminary talks for TSMC to possibly own and operate a Texas Terafab factory or supply technology.

4.text: TSMC is evaluating a new Texas campus with multiple fabs costing at least $20 billion each, on top of its $265 billion Arizona commitment (raised by $100 billion in July). Other articles note AMD's market value now exceeds Intel's by 60%, and TSMC 2nm capacity may drive equipment spending.

5.text: Applied Materials and Qualcomm are compared with ASML on valuation, revenue trends, and risk, with ASML noted for its near-monopoly on advanced chip printing. TSMC is not mentioned; the articles bear on it only as ASML's main High-NA EUV customer.
